items.title: Jensen Huang’s exit puts Nvidia’s support for open source in question
items.snippet: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned Thursday after he admitted to an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, raising concerns about U.S. national security and the motives behind the executive’s support for softer chip export controls on China. Huang has been a staunch supporter of open source AI, framing the ecosystem as good for safety, innovation, diffusion, and sovereignty. And as frontier AI labs increasingly move to reduce their reliance on Nvidia and build their own chips, supporting open source is also a good way for the company to diversify its customer base by selling chips to nation-states, enterprises, and any organization that wants to own its own models. Still, Huang’s resignation raises questions about whether Nvidia will carry on his legacy by continuing to support the open model community. Jensen no longer being CEO would be very very bad for the open model cause in the US. Huang’s departure also comes as Nvidia has yet to finalize a deal to acquire open source platform Hugging Face for $13 billion. items.title: Samsung settles four-year Wireless PowerShare patent lawsuit
items.snippet: Samsung has settled a US patent infringement lawsuit over the Wireless PowerShare feature on its Galaxy phones. The company, wireless charging chip supplier Renesas Electronics America, and WiPQTUS recently submitted a joint agreement, withdrawing all claims as part of an out-of-court settlement. Wireless PowerShare lets you charge compatible Galaxy Watches, Galaxy Buds, other Galaxy phones, and Qi-compatible devices by placing them on the back of your handset. The feature first showed up on the Galaxy S10 in 2019, and the complaint also named phones from the Galaxy S20, S21, and S22...

When Google Fi first launched in 2015, users were originally able to switch between T-Mobile and Sprint's networks. items.title: Siri AI Coming to Older Apple TV 4K Models in tvOS 27.2.1
items.snippet: An upcoming tvOS 27.2.1 update will bring Siri AI to the 2nd- and 3rd-generation Apple TV 4K models, according to Apple. items.title: Apple Explains How HomeView Keeps Camera Data Private
items.snippet: Apple today shared an in-depth look at how it's using Secure Exclaves to protect camera and microphone data on the HomeView, iPhone 18 Pro , and other products. items.snippet: Steven Levy at Wired, in a terrific post-event follow-up to his exclusive early look at the new MacBook Pros ( News+ link ): I first met Ternus in 2015, when I spent a day with him at Apple’s Input Design Lab, a testing facility in Cupertino. items.title: OurCal
items.snippet: My thanks to OurCal for sponsoring last week at DF. You ever have a discussion that starts with “I didn’t see you put that on the calendar”? Could be with your colleagues, could be with your family. But the problem is familiar: Shared calendars solved scheduling, not communication. OurCal connects any calendar, new or existing, to a group chat. Changes post there automatically, so nobody misses them. Because it’s a messenger, they made everything end-to-end encrypted, certified by France’s cybersecurity agency. OurCal is native SwiftUI across Apple’s platforms, and the App Store just featured it in “Great apps on iPhone Duo”. They’ve got an Android app too, but they’re an Apple-first company

items.title: Safari 27.3 Adds Support for Global Privacy Control
items.snippet: Nick Heer, Pixel Envy: There are a whole bunch of features and fixes coming to Safari with Apple’s OS 27.3 update. One that is not in the beta release notes but appears nevertheless is support for Global Privacy Control . This new standard is effectively a replacement for Do Not Track with legal muscle that should permit you to indicate your tracking preference one time and then, theoretically, never again see a cookie consent banner. ★

items.title: Every time you click a link, Windows 11 quietly launches a second copy of your browser just to pass it along, and Firefox is now testing Microsoft’s fix
items.snippet: A Mozilla patch, still off by default, lets Windows 11 send links and Start menu launches to a running Firefox without spawning another firefox.exe. Edge 150 already does this, and the November Patch Tuesday update brings it to every eligible PC, with Chromium browsers possibly next. items.title: Cisco Live Melbourne: AI agents will break today’s enterprise network, and Cisco wants to rebuild it
items.snippet: To date, AI conversations have centered on GPUs, AI factories, and data centers. At Cisco Live APJC in Melbourne this week, Cisco shifted the focus to the campus, the branch, and the network that connects everything. The opening keynote set a realistic tone for where the industry is. Agents don’t behave like people, and networks built for people won’t hold up when thousands of agents work around the clock. items.title: Oracle cancels $7 billion Tencent AI chip deal
items.snippet: Oracle has reportedly cancelled a five-year agreement to lease advanced artificial intelligence computing capacity to Chinese technology giant Tencent , following concerns raised by the Trump administration over the deal’s implications for U.S. technology export restrictions. The agreement was estimated to be worth $7 billion. It would have provided Tencent with access to approximately 100,000 advanced Nvidia AI chips installed in data centers across Southeast Asia. The cancellation was reported by the Financial Times and others , citing people familiar with the matter. items.title: Data center champions lose badly as ballot initiatives target AI infrastructure
items.snippet: Republicans weren’t the only group taking it on the chin in midterm elections. Data centers and their supporters got positively annihilated at elections across the country. These concerns are reflected in public opinion. The data center development opponents won and won big. A University of Massachusetts Amherst poll cited by Stateline found that just 11% of Americans supported building an AI data center in their community.
